rationale: Both candidates almost entirely miss the ground truth's core concerns (insufficient validation evidence, native-speed/streaming HTTP-vs-WebSocket asymmetry, talker/decoder bounds duplication, benchmark harness registry design) — X gets weak partial credit via a serving_speech.py:3642 test-coverage note in the right topic area but misses the actual asymmetry bug, while Y never touches streaming/speed validation or the benchmark discussion at all. X's findings (pytest marker hygiene, CI gate status, doc-ordering nit) are narrow but highly verifiable and low-risk. Y is a much deeper, more actionable engineering review with concrete diffs and real architectural risks (uninitialized bias, silent zero-audio fallback, concat-semantics bug), though several claims rest on internal implementation details not visible in the diff and carry more unverifiable risk. Given comparable weak recall, Y's substance and actionability edge it out narrowly.
